page: Vultr vcg-a16-3c-32g-8vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with 3 shared vCPUs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system features 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB per core. Graphics and parallel computing acceleration are delivered via a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU, providing 0.5 of a physical GPU and 8 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 170 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear division between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance of 1705.53 and single-threaded gzip compression of 26.06 GB/sec fall into the average tier. However, multi-core CPU performance of 5059.76 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 29.11 GB/sec are weak, reflecting the shared CPU allocation. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 35.06 GB/sec and a Passmark memory score of 1768.52, both ranking in the bottom 25 percent.

For machine learning workloads, the fractional NVIDIA A16 GPU supports average inference speeds on small models, achieving 549.08 tokens per second for prompt processing and 125.03 tokens per second for text generation on a 135M parameter model. Performance drops significantly on larger architectures, with a 7B model yielding poor results of 11.05 tokens per second for prompt processing. Consequently, this server is suited for small-scale model inference, lightweight GPU-accelerated development, and basic media processing rather than large-scale LLM deployment or high-throughput database operations.

The instance is capable of handling smaller machine learning tasks, achieving average inference speeds of 125.03 tokens per second for text generation on a 135M parameter model, though performance degrades on larger 7B models. This hardware profile offers a cost-efficient entry point for lightweight GPU-accelerated workloads, small-scale model inference, and development environments, while being less suited for intensive database operations or heavy multi-threaded computing.
